_contractVersion: v1 anchored pins in transcript-line space (scrollLine/scrollBase). v2 (R17) anchors them in RENDER-POSITION space — array position over row count — because that is the space the rail actually lays rows out in, and it is the space the focus tab already used. A rig reads this field to know which shape it holds; a rig still expecting v1 must not silently consume v2 fracs.

contiguous._: The easy ledger: array position i holds T(i+1). Turn-number space and render space AGREE here, which is exactly why the v1 bug went unnoticed.

nonContiguous._: THE R17 REGRESSION. A real ledger shape — 19 of 125 look like this: turn numbers have gaps, so array position 113 holds T113 while the last index is 124. Render space and turn-number space diverge, and a marker anchored the old way lands where a NUMBER implies instead of on a drawn row. 118 rows: T1..T113 then T116, T118, T119, T121, T124.

expected._: T113 is the 113th row → position 112 of 118. The OLD formula said 113/124 ≈ 0.911; a whole row and more of drift.
The last drawn row, whatever number it carries.

undrawn._: A turn number the gaps swallowed. No row carries T117, so a pin naming it is OMITTED — never clamped to a neighbour, because a V-number shown against the wrong checkpoint is a wrong version (R8).

coLocated._: ONE space, TWO anchors. A turn row and a pin naming the same checkpoint share a frac — that is the F6 pair to screenshot. A trace boundary does NOT: afterIndex names the checkpoint it comes AFTER, so it sits at the edge below that row. Anchoring it on the row drew every boundary one row early.

endMarker._: A boundary after the LAST row is the bottom of the rail. Render-position anchoring dropped it to (n-1)/n = 0.75 and left the end-of-transcript marker floating one row short; the rail original afterIndex/lastIndex landed on 1, and this is the render-space equivalent.

empty._: No rows drawn yet (terminal just attached, or a fresh install pinned before its first turn): pins are omitted, never guessed onto the rail.
